businessModel: Executive search and staffing firm serving financial services and technology sectors
sourceNote: Real-world case from recruiting/staffing sector. Business context reflects typical recruiting firm facing utilization and talent retention challenges.

ownerIntake.businessType: Executive search and staffing firm specializing in financial services and tech hiring. Founded 2008, 150 employees (120 recruiters, 30 support), 45 offices across major US markets. Placed 800+ professionals in 2024.
ownerIntake.stage: Growth stage: $45M revenue (15% YoY growth, slowing from 25% growth two years ago), EBITDA $6.8M (15% margin, down from 18% two years ago), utilization 78% (down from 82% two years ago). Recruiter productivity declining: revenue per recruiter $300k (down from $340k two years ago). Margin pressure from rising recruiter salaries (+18% in last 18 months).
ownerIntake.ownerGoal: Return to 20%+ EBITDA margin and demonstrate profitability leverage within 18 months to support Series B fund-raising or strategic acquisition.
ownerConstraints: Talent market: Recruiting market highly competitive for top talent. Recruiter turnover 20% annually (vs. 12% two years ago); rising retention costs. Offers market competitive but margin-constrained.

Utilization and productivity: Utilization 78% (declining from 82%) suggests bench time increasing or client work declining. Productivity per recruiter declining. Difficult to scale profitably without addressing utilization.
Competitive pressure: Tech and fintech companies hiring directly (not through recruiters), reducing recruiter-dependent hiring. Reduced demand for high-end executive search in certain verticals.
Economic sensitivity: Tech hiring (major segment) sensitive to economic cycles. Current macro uncertainty is impacting hiring budgets.
Scale economics: $45M revenue is below scale-efficient size for profitability; competitor consolidation creating larger, more efficient players.
ownerIntake.immediateConcern: Growth stalling (15% current vs. 25% two years ago) while margins compressing (15% current vs. 18%). Recruiter productivity declining (revenue per recruiter down 12% in two years), suggesting either client demand softening or recruiter efficiency declining. Salary costs rising 18% while revenue per recruiter falling, creating a profitability squeeze. Must determine whether problem is demand-driven (fewer placements), supply-driven (recruiter productivity), or structural (market shift away from recruiting firm model).

businessProblem: A specialized recruiting firm is experiencing simultaneous growth slowdown (15% current vs. 25% two years ago) and margin compression (15% EBITDA vs. 18%), driven by declining recruiter productivity (revenue per recruiter $300k vs. $340k two years ago) and rising salary costs (+18%). Management must determine whether the problem is demand-driven (client hiring budget constraints due to macro uncertainty), supply-driven (recruiter efficiency or retention issues), or structural (market shift away from recruiter-dependent hiring). Without clarity, Series B fund-raising or strategic acquisition will be difficult.

evidence.finding: Growth decelerating (15% YoY current vs. 25% growth two years ago) while margins compressing (15% EBITDA vs. 18%). Revenue per recruiter declining 12% (from $340k to $300k) in two years, suggesting either recruiter productivity falling or bench time increasing. Salary costs rising 18% in 18 months, outpacing revenue growth.
evidence.source: Financial statements, staffing metrics, utilization analysis

evidence.finding: Utilization declining from 82% to 78%, suggesting increased bench time. Recruiter turnover rising to 20% annually (from 12% two years ago), indicating talent retention challenge. Productivity decline could be due to recruiter churn (less experienced team), market conditions (harder to place), or client demand softening.
evidence.source: Utilization reports, HR metrics, project tracking

evidence.finding: Tech hiring (45% of revenue) growing 18% YoY (healthy), but fintech (40% of revenue) growing only 8% (slower), reflecting macro sensitivity. Executive search premium segment, but junior-mid placement (65% of core) more competitive. Competitive pressure from tech companies hiring directly and larger recruiting firms consolidating.
evidence.source: Revenue mix analysis, market trends, competitive intelligence
